title: A Deterministic and Auditable AI Security Risk Assessment Framework with ATLAS Aligned Executable Rules and Formal Verification
abstract: arXiv:2610.01436v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems are increasingly deployed in high impact and safety critical settings, yet security assessment remains difficult to reproduce and defend under audit. Existing approaches often rely on narrative checklists or assessor driven scoring, and they lack an explicit, machine evaluable mapping from observable engineering artefacts to stable technique level outcomes. We present an evidence driven AI security assessment framework that operationalises assessment as a deterministic decision function. The framework normalises heterogeneous artefacts into a project independent Control ID taxonomy scored on a bounded four level ordinal scale, compiles technique level predicates from a pinned MITRE ATLAS snapshot via an explicit mitigation to control mapping, and outputs technique indexed feasibility and impact levels with traceable links back to the triggering evidence. translated_title: 一种基于ATLAS对齐可执行规则与形式化验证的确定性、可审计AI安全风险评估框架
translated_abstract: 人工智能系统正越来越多地部署于高影响、安全攸关的场景中，然而安全评估在审计条件下仍难以复现和辩护。现有方法往往依赖叙述性清单或评估者主导的打分，缺乏从可观测的工程制品到稳定的技术层面结果的显式、可机器求值的映射。我们提出了一个证据驱动的AI安全评估框架，将评估操作化为一个确定性决策函数。该框架将异构制品规范化为与项目无关的控制ID分类体系，并采用有界的四级序数量表进行打分；通过显式的缓解措施到控制的映射，从固定的MITRE ATLAS快照编译技术层面的谓词；输出以技术为索引的可行性与影响级别，并提供可追溯回触发证据的链接。我们将所有规范性选择打包为带版本的评估……
tldr: 该论文提出一个证据驱动的AI安全评估框架，将安全评估操作化为确定性决策函数，通过控制ID分类体系、由固定MITRE ATLAS快照编译的可执行规则以及形式化验证，实现可复现、可审计且证据可追溯的技术级风险评估。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an evidence-driven AI security assessment framework that operationalizes assessment as a deterministic decision function, using a project-independent Control ID taxonomy, executable rules compiled from a pinned MITRE ATLAS snapshot, and formal verification to achieve reproducible, auditable, and evidence-traceable technique-level risk evaluation.
